sections.html:
Woodburn is a Marion County city at the northern end of the Willamette Valley, about 17 miles north-northeast of Salem and 30 miles south-southwest of Portland. Interstate 5 runs along its edge, and many residents commute out of town.

Population is 31,948 as of July 1, 2025, up from 26,013 in 2020. Buyers touring a Woodburn house in a market growing that fast tend to arrive with specific expectations, and the city includes a mix of households, among them multigenerational families.

Woodburn splits roughly two to one between owners and renters, and households run larger than the national average.

About 36% of occupied homes are rented. If you own a rental, a tenant in place changes how and when the house can be shown or closed.

Woodburn also has what is described as the largest 55-plus retirement community in Oregon, with 1,510 single-family homes and a private golf course. A home inside an age-restricted community follows that community’s own rules, so read its governing documents before you set a timeline.

sections.h2: Permits that can surface at inspection
sections.html:
Woodburn requires a building permit for several kinds of work that owners often finish without one. A buyer’s inspector may notice. Permits are required for:

  • Adding a bedroom or finishing an attic, garage or basement into living space
  • Cutting new window or door openings, or widening existing ones
  • Adding or moving walls, or building a stairway
  • Reroofing where old roofing is removed and new sheathing is installed
  • A carport, garage or shed over 200 square feet or 15 feet tall
  • A deck or porch floor more than 30 inches above grade

Mechanical permits cover woodstoves, fireplace inserts, gas piping and vented fans. Building and mechanical permits go through Woodburn City Hall at 270 Montgomery Street or Oregon ePermitting. Electrical and plumbing permits go through Marion County Public Works at 503-588-5036.

An unpermitted ADU has a path forward. Such units can be legalized if they meet zoning, building code and public works standards under Woodburn Development Ordinance section 2.07.20. An ADU may not exceed 50% of the main home’s floor area or 725 square feet, whichever is less, and must connect to city water and sewer. The city also allows duplexes and other middle housing in all residential zones.

If you have one, say so at the start of any sale conversation. A buyer who purchases as-is can decide whether to legalize it, and raising it yourself is easier than explaining it after the title report arrives.

Complaints about overgrown weeds, or an abandoned property that is a fire or safety hazard, go through the Woodburn Police Department at 503-982-2345. A neglected yard on a vacant house is a common reason owners hear from the city, so keep the lot tidy while the sale is pending.

The city bills water and sewer, and the Finance Department at 503-982-5222 handles accounts. A typical single-family home pays minimum charges of about $19 a month for water and about $52 a month for sewer, even at zero use.

If the house will sit empty during a sale, water can be suspended for at least 30 days for a $35 fee. The city advises keeping water on in winter and for any home with automatic sprinklers. A property manager can handle the account with a signed Property Management Agreement filed with Finance.

Marion County bills Woodburn property tax, and the Tax Collection office in Salem sends statements between October 15 and 25. Oregon’s tax year runs from July 1 to June 30, and the main due date is November 15.

  • Pay in full by November 15 for a 3% discount.
  • Pay two-thirds by November 15 for a 2% discount on that amount, with the last third due May 15.
  • Pay one-third with no discount, with the next thirds due February 15 and May 15.
  • Payments postmarked after November 15 lose discounts and owe interest.

Marion County’s Tax Collection office is at 555 Court Street NE, Suite 2242, Salem. Reach it at 503-588-5215 or propertytax@co.marion.or.us. If you think the county’s real market value is too high, the Property Value Appeals Board accepts petitions between the date statements are mailed and December 31.

The escrow agent works out each side’s share. For closings from mid-October through June 30, the seller has usually paid that year’s taxes and the buyer reimburses a portion from the agreed date, typically closing or possession. For closings between July 1 and mid-October, the seller credits the buyer a prorated share based on the prior year’s tax.

Unpaid taxes do not go away. Oregon law allows foreclosure of real property once three years have gone by since the earliest delinquency, and the county then holds the property for two years after judgment unless it is redeemed first. Selling earlier keeps more choices open, and a back-tax balance is normally paid from your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Why Woodburn owners look for a quick sale
sections.html: People who contact a cash buyer here usually have a practical problem that a standard listing handles slowly: a tenant in place, an inherited house with several heirs, work done without a permit, or a gap between what the house needs and what the owner can spend. With about 36% of occupied homes rented, tenant-occupied sales are routine. Homes in the age-restricted community carry that community’s own approval steps.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of a Woodburn house works
sections.html:
A cash sale follows the same escrow path as any Oregon closing, minus a lender’s appraisal and underwriting. The title company opens escrow, orders a title report, orders payoff demands for any liens, collects signatures and funds, and records the deed with the county.

Monetary liens are generally cleared through escrow, so the buyer takes title free of them, and a seller pays any liens or judgments against that seller. If a back-tax balance or an unpermitted ADU is part of your situation, tell the buyer early.

faqs.q: What county is Woodburn, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Woodburn is in Marion County, so the county bills and collects your property tax. The Tax Collection office is in Salem and its number is 503-588-5215.

faqs.q: When are Woodburn property taxes due?
faqs.a: The main due date is November 15. Paying the full amount by then earns a 3% discount, paying two-thirds earns 2% on that amount, and paying one-third earns no discount. Later installments are due February 15 and May 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Woodburn house with an unpermitted ADU?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions about it. The city says an unpermitted ADU can be legalized if it meets zoning, building code and public works standards. A buyer who purchases as-is can decide whether to legalize it.

faqs.q: Who do I call about an overgrown yard or abandoned house in Woodburn?
faqs.a: Call the Woodburn Police Department's code enforcement line at 503-982-2345. It handles overgrown weeds and abandoned property that is a fire or safety hazard.

faqs.q: What happens if I stop paying property tax on a Woodburn house?
faqs.a: The county can begin foreclosure once three years have gone by since the earliest delinquency. After a foreclosure judgment, the county holds the property for two years before redemption rights end, so selling earlier keeps more options open.
